name_en: bonito — the fast-swimming icon of early-summer Japan
summary_ja: 黒潮に乗って北上する回遊魚で、初夏の初鰹はあっさりと脂が少なく、秋に南下する戻り鰹は脂がのって濃厚になる。藁の香ばしさをまとわせた「たたき」や刺身で食べられ、黒潮に近い港ほど鮮度と旨みが際立つとされる。
summary_en: A migratory fish riding the Kuroshio current north each spring, lean in early summer and richer once it turns south in autumn. Seared with straw as tataki or served raw, with flavor prized most near the ports the current runs closest to.

name_en: chum salmon — the fish that returns to its home river
summary_ja: 生まれた川に戻る性質を持つ回遊魚。北の海で育つほど脂がのり、塩鮭・新巻鮭・いくらと身も卵も余さず使われる。産卵前の遡上時期に川筋の港で揚がるものほど、脂と身の締まりの両方が評価される。
summary_en: A migratory fish that returns to spawn in its home river, fattening the longer it feeds in northern seas. Salted, dried as aramaki, or taken for ikura roe — river-mouth ports landing it just before the spawning run prize both its fat and firm flesh.

name_en: mackerel — an everyday fish prized when the fat runs high
summary_ja: 秋から冬にかけて脂がのる青魚で、塩焼き・味噌煮・しめさばと調理法が幅広い。速い潮に揉まれて回遊せず居着いた個体は身が締まり脂も強く、そうした産地ではブランド名を掲げて一本釣りで水揚げされる。
summary_en: A blue-backed fish fattest from autumn into winter, grilled with salt, simmered in miso, or vinegar-cured. Fish held still by fast currents rather than migrating firm up and fatten further, giving rise to named, pole-and-line branded catches.

name_en: horse mackerel — the fish behind Japan's everyday fry and sashimi
summary_ja: 一年中出回る青魚で、刺身・たたき・フライと家庭料理の定番。回遊せず一つの海域に居着いた個体は速い潮流にもまれて身が締まり脂もよくのるため、そうした漁場では高級ブランドとして一本釣りされる。
summary_en: A blue-backed fish sold year-round, served raw, minced as tataki, or fried. Fish that settle in one fast-flowing strait rather than migrate firm up and fatten, and are pole-and-line caught there under premium regional brand names.

name_en: sardine — a small, oil-rich fish central to everyday cooking and dashi
summary_ja: 群れで回遊する小型の青魚で、刺身・梅煮・つみれと安価に食べられる。脂の質は漁場の潮境に左右され、寒流と暖流がぶつかる海域に面した港ほど水揚げ量が多く、乾燥させれば出汁の要となる煮干しになる。
summary_en: A small, schooling blue-backed fish eaten raw, simmered with plum, or as tsumire dumplings. Its fat quality tracks the tidal boundary it feeds along, and ports facing where cold and warm currents meet land the most — dried, it becomes niboshi dashi stock.

name_en: Pacific saury — the fish that announces autumn with smoke and salt
summary_ja: 秋に旬を迎える細長い回遊魚で、内臓ごと丸ごと塩焼きにするのが定番。群れが接岸する海域に面した港ほど水揚げが多く、脂の乗りと苦みのある内臓の風味が、その年その港の漁模様を映すとされる。
summary_en: A slender migratory fish at its peak in autumn, traditionally grilled whole with salt, innards included. Ports facing waters where the shoals come close to shore land the most, and the fat and bitter innards are said to reflect that year's catch.

name_en: yellowtail — a winter fish whose name changes as it grows
summary_ja: 成長に伴い呼び名が変わる出世魚で、冬に脂がのった「寒ブリ」は刺身・照り焼き・ぶり大根で好まれる。越冬前に湾内で脂を蓄えてから定置網で揚がる産地ほど、脂の質と歩留まりの高さが評価される。
summary_en: A 'shusseuo' whose name changes with size. Winter's fat-laden 'kanburi' is prized raw, teriyaki-glazed, or simmered with daikon — bays where it fattens before wintering, then is taken in set nets, are valued for both fat quality and yield.

name_en: greater amberjack — a firmer, leaner relative of yellowtail
summary_ja: ブリに似るが身が締まり脂は控えめな高級魚で、夏が旬とされる。天然物は黒潮に近い海域で獲れ、養殖物は穏やかな湾内で育てられるため、産地によって身の締まりと脂のりの傾向が異なるとされる。
summary_en: Related to yellowtail but firmer and leaner, at its best in summer. Wild fish come from Kuroshio-adjacent waters while farmed ones grow in calm bays, so firmness and fat content vary noticeably by where the fish was raised.

name_en: yellowtail amberjack — a summer fish valued above buri by many chefs
summary_ja: ブリに似た姿だが体高があり平たく、夏が旬の高級魚。回遊性が強く黒潮沿いの島嶼部で漁獲されることが多く、寿司職人の間ではその身質からブリより上とされることもある。
summary_en: Similar in shape to yellowtail but taller-bodied and flatter, at its best in summer. Strongly migratory, it is mostly taken around Kuroshio-adjacent islands, and some sushi chefs rank its texture above buri.

name_en: red seabream — the celebratory fish of Japan
summary_ja: 祝いの席に欠かせない紅い魚で、淡白な白身は刺身・鯛めし・塩焼きと幅広く使われる。速い潮流にもまれて身が締まる天然物と、穏やかな湾で育てる養殖物とで、産地ごとに食感の評価が分かれる。
summary_en: The red fish central to Japanese celebrations. Its mild white flesh appears raw, in taimeshi rice, or salt-grilled — wild fish firmed by fast currents and farmed fish raised in calm bays earn distinct reputations by region.

name_en: olive flounder — a lean, prized winter flatfish
summary_ja: 「左ヒラメに右カレイ」で見分ける平たい魚で、冬に脂がのる。荒波にもまれて育つ天然物はコリコリとした食感が強く、刺身では薄造りにして昆布締めにすると旨みが増すとされる高級魚。
summary_en: The flatfish distinguished from karei by 'eyes on the left', at its best in winter. Wild fish raised in rough surf develop a notably firm, chewy bite, and thin-sliced sashimi is often kombu-cured to deepen its flavor.

name_en: flounder — a broad family of flatfish eaten simmered or fried
summary_ja: 「左ヒラメに右カレイ」で見分ける平たい魚の総称で、煮付けや唐揚げで親しまれる。冷たい海域で育つ種類ほど脂がのりやすく、種類ごとに旬も産地も異なるため、選び方一つで食味が変わるとされる。
summary_en: A broad family of flatfish, distinguished from hirame by 'eyes on the right'. Enjoyed simmered or deep-fried — colder-water species tend to run fattier, and both season and source vary widely across the many types sold under this name.

name_en: Pacific cod — a winter fish whose name means 'plenty'
summary_ja: 「たらふく食べる」の語源とされる冬の魚で、鍋の具、白子、たらこの親としても親しまれる。冷たい海峡に面した港では昆布〆にする文化が根付き、身の淡白さを引き立てる保存の知恵が伝わる。
summary_en: A winter fish said to give Japanese the phrase 'eat one's fill'. Its mild flesh goes into hot pots, and it yields both shirako milt and the roe for tarako — cold-strait ports developed kombu-curing to draw out flavor from its plain flesh.

name_en: Okhotsk atka mackerel — the grilled fish of Hokkaido izakaya
summary_ja: 北海道の居酒屋で開きの塩焼きとして親しまれる魚で、冷たい親潮の海域で育つほど脂がのりやすい。鮮魚での流通が難しいため一夜干しの開き干しにする加工文化が発達し、旨みが凝縮されるとされる。
summary_en: The fish behind Hokkaido izakaya's split, salt-grilled classic. It fattens more in the cold Oyashio current, and because it travels poorly fresh, an overnight-dried himono tradition developed that is said to concentrate its flavor.

name_en: herring — the fish that built Hokkaido's coastal fortunes
summary_ja: 明治から昭和初期に大漁が続き、北海道沿岸に「鰊御殿」を建てた魚で、数の子はその卵にあたる。群れの産卵で海が白く染まるほどの豊漁だった歴史が、身欠きニシンなど保存加工の文化を今に残す。
summary_en: The fish behind Hokkaido's 'herring mansions', built on booming catches from the Meiji era into early Showa. Its roe is kazunoko, and a history of shoals so dense spawning turned the sea white lives on in dried mikaki-nishin preservation.

name_en: Japanese shishamo — a small autumn fish caught only off Hokkaido's Pacific coast
summary_ja: 北海道太平洋沿岸のみに生息する小魚で、子持ちししゃもとして丸ごと焼いて食べる秋の味覚。生息域が限られるため漁期は河口への遡上時のみに限られ、本物は流通量が少なく別種の輸入品と区別される。
summary_en: A small fish found only off Hokkaido's Pacific coast. Grilled whole, roe and all, as an autumn specialty — its limited habitat confines the season to the river-mouth run, so the genuine article is scarce and distinct from imported look-alikes.

name_en: freshwater eel — grilled and glazed for a summer stamina meal
summary_ja: 蒲焼として夏の土用の丑の日に食べられる魚で、関東は背開きで蒸してから焼き、関西は腹開きで直焼きにする。シラスウナギが豊富に獲れた汽水湖のほとりでは、養鰻業が発達し名物として定着した。
summary_en: Grilled and glazed as kabayaki, traditionally eaten on the midsummer Day of the Ox for stamina. Eastern Japan steams before grilling while the west grills straight through — towns by brackish lakes rich in glass eels built eel-farming into local fame.

name_en: sweetfish — a river fish with the scent of watermelon
summary_ja: 清流の石についた苔を食む川魚で、西瓜に似た独特の香りを持つ。塩焼きや友釣りの対象として夏を代表し、水の透明度が高い川ほど香りが際立つとされ、清流の名を冠したブランド鮎も多い。
summary_en: A river fish that grazes algae off clean streambed stones, giving it a distinct watermelon-like scent. Salt-grilled and famously caught by tomo-zuri decoy fishing — the clearer the river, the more that scent is said to stand out.

name_en: char — the trout of Japan's remotest mountain streams
summary_ja: 渓流の最上流部に棲む川魚で、警戒心が強く岩陰に隠れることが名の由来ともされる。人里から離れた冷たい源流部ほど生息し、塩焼きにすると淡白な身に上品な脂がにじむ渓流釣りの人気魚。
summary_en: A river char living in the uppermost reaches of mountain streams, said to take its name from hiding wary among rocks. Found in the coldest, most remote headwaters, and salt-grilled to bring out a delicate fat within its mild flesh.

name_en: red-spotted masu trout — the landlocked form of cherry salmon
summary_ja: サクラマスが川に残留した陸封型で、渓流釣りの人気対象。塩焼きにすると身の締まりと上品な脂が楽しめ、冷たく澄んだ源流に生息するほど体側の朱点が鮮やかになるとされる美しい川魚。
summary_en: The landlocked form of cherry salmon, a favorite of stream anglers. Salt-grilled, it offers firm flesh and delicate fat, and its trademark red spots are said to grow more vivid the colder and clearer the headwater stream.

name_en: rainbow trout — an introduced trout now farmed across Japan
summary_ja: 北米原産で明治期に移入された川魚で、養殖が全国に広がった。湧水を使う養殖場では水温が安定するため一年を通して身が締まりやすく、塩焼きやフライのほか刺身でも食べられる。
summary_en: A trout native to North America, introduced to Japan in the Meiji era and now farmed nationwide. Spring-fed farms hold a steady temperature that keeps flesh firm year-round, and it is served salt-grilled, fried, or even raw.

name_en: tiger pufferfish — the prized, licensed fish of winter
summary_ja: 毒を持つため調理には専門免許が必要な高級魚で、薄造りの刺身「てっさ」や鍋で食べられる。速い海峡の潮流にもまれる海域で育つ個体は身の締まりが強く、市場が集まる港ほど処理の技術が磨かれてきた。
summary_en: A premium fish whose toxin requires a licensed chef to prepare. Sliced paper-thin as tessa sashimi or simmered in hot pot — fish raised in fast strait currents firm up notably, and ports with large markets refined the knife skill needed to serve it safely.

name_en: pike conger — the summer fish of Kyoto's Gion Festival
summary_ja: 小骨が多く骨切りの技術を要する魚で、梅雨の水を飲んで美味くなるとされる。京都の祇園祭に欠かせない夏の味とされ、京へ運びやすい近海の産地ほど需要が集まり、骨切りの技が磨かれてきた。
summary_en: A fish so fine-boned it demands the knife skill of hone-kiri, said to fatten on the rains of early summer. Essential to Kyoto's Gion Festival, nearby coastal grounds able to supply the city quickly saw demand concentrate and the craft sharpen.

name_en: beltfish — a silver, sword-shaped fish eaten grilled or fried
summary_ja: 銀色に光る太刀のような細長い魚で、皮ごと食べられる。塩焼きやムニエルで脂の乗った身を楽しみ、黒潮に近い海域で一本釣りされる型の大きな個体ほど脂のりが良く、高値で取引される。
summary_en: A long, silver-bladed fish eaten skin and all. Salt-grilled or pan-fried to bring out its fatty flesh — larger fish taken by pole-and-line near the Kuroshio current run fattier still and command higher prices.

name_en: splendid alfonsino — a deep-red fish prized for its rich fat
summary_ja: 深海に棲む鮮やかな赤い魚で、脂の乗りが良く煮付けや刺身にされる。急に深くなる海底が漁場となる沿岸では一本釣りが伝わり、船から港までの距離が近いほど鮮度を保ったまま高値で出荷できるとされる。
summary_en: A vivid red deep-sea fish, richly fatty when simmered or served raw. Coasts where the seabed drops away steeply support pole-and-line fishing close to shore, and the short trip back to port helps land it fresh enough to fetch premium prices.

name_en: blackthroat seaperch — a deep-red fish nicknamed 'nodoguro' for its black throat
summary_ja: 喉の奥が黒いことからの通称を持つ深海魚で、脂が乗り、あぶり寿司や塩焼きで高級魚として扱われる。日本海側の急深な地形に面した港では一本釣りや底引き網で揚がり、地域ブランドとして売られる。
summary_en: A deep-sea fish nicknamed for the black patch inside its throat. Rich and fatty, served as seared sushi or salt-grilled — ports facing the Sea of Japan's steep seabed land it by pole-and-line and trawl, selling it under regional brand names.

name_en: barracuda — a slender fish best known dried
summary_ja: 細長い体をした沿岸魚で、水分が多く身が傷みやすいため干物にすると旨みが増すとされる。港に近い漁場で獲れてすぐ加工できる産地ほど、干物としての評価が高くなる傾向がある。
summary_en: A slender coastal fish whose watery flesh spoils quickly, so drying it into himono is said to concentrate its flavor. Places able to process the catch near the fishing grounds tend to earn the strongest reputation for their dried fish.

name_en: Spanish mackerel — a slender fish central to Setouchi's spring table
summary_ja: 「魚へんに春」と書く字の通り春が旬の細長い魚で、西京焼きや刺身で食べられる。瀬戸内海の穏やかな内海で回遊が滞留しやすく、水揚げの多い産地では祭り寿司の具として食文化に根付いている。
summary_en: Its kanji combines 'fish' and 'spring' — a slender fish at its best that season, served miso-glazed or raw. It tends to linger in the calm Seto Inland Sea, and top-landing areas there have folded it into their festival sushi culture.

name_en: flying fish — a lean summer fish that leaps from the water
summary_ja: 胸びれを広げて海面を飛ぶように滑空する魚で、あっさりした白身は焼き物になる。傷みが早いため沿岸で獲れてすぐ干して焼く加工が発達し、その乾物はあごだしとして出汁文化を支えている。
summary_en: A fish that glides above the waves on outstretched pectoral fins. Its lean white flesh is grilled, and because it spoils fast, coastal towns developed a grill-then-dry method whose product, 'ago', underpins a whole dashi tradition.

name_en: Japanese whiting — a light summer fish taken from sandy shallows
summary_ja: 砂地の浅瀬に棲む白身魚で、天ぷらのネタとして知られる。淡白でクセがなく身が薄いため揚げても火が通りやすく、遠浅の内湾に面した産地では投げ釣りの対象魚としても親しまれてきた。
summary_en: A white-fleshed fish of sandy shallows, best known as a tempura staple. Mild and thin-fleshed, it fries through quickly, and shallow-bay towns have also long prized it as a favorite target for shore anglers.

name_en: rockfish — a bulge-eyed fish that signals spring
summary_ja: 目が大きく突き出た岩礁性の魚で、春を告げる魚とされる。煮付けで骨まで味を含ませて食べるのが定番で、瀬戸内海の岩礁域など潮通しの良い漁場に面した土地では県の魚に定めるほど食文化に根付く。
summary_en: A large-eyed fish of rocky reefs, said to herald spring. Traditionally simmered until the seasoning reaches the bone — areas facing well-flushed rocky grounds like the Seto Inland Sea have woven it deeply into local food culture.

name_en: marbled rockfish — a spiny, big-headed fish for soup and stew
summary_ja: 岩礁に棲む頭の大きな魚で、骨から出汁が出るため煮付けや潮汁で丸ごと使われる。動きが少なく居着く性質のため漁場ごとに味の個体差が出やすく、地元で消費される地魚として扱われることが多い。
summary_en: A big-headed fish of rocky reefs whose bones give off a rich stock, so it is often simmered or served whole in clear soup. Sedentary by nature, it varies noticeably by fishing ground and is mostly eaten as a local catch near where it's landed.

name_en: monkfish — a winter fish famously hung and carved for its liver
summary_ja: 冬に脂が乗る深海魚で、吊るし切りという独特の解体法で捌かれる。あん肝と鍋の具として食べられ、黒潮と親潮がぶつかる好漁場に面した港ほど水揚げが多く、鍋文化として根付いてきた。
summary_en: A winter deep-sea fish, traditionally carved by hanging it whole. Prized for its liver, ankimo, and for hot pot — ports facing where the Kuroshio and Oyashio currents meet land the most, and built the fish into a hot-pot tradition.

name_en: longtooth grouper — a rare, prized winter grouper
summary_ja: 「幻の魚」とも呼ばれる大型のハタ科の魚で、冬に旬を迎え鍋や刺身で高値がつく。黒潮に面したリアス式の岩場は稚魚の隠れ場となるため、天然物も養殖物もその海域の産地が中心となっている。
summary_en: A large grouper sometimes called the 'phantom fish' for its scarcity. At its best in winter, commanding high prices raw or in hot pot — Kuroshio-facing ria coastlines shelter its juveniles, so both wild and farmed fish center on those waters.

name_en: grouper — a broad family of warm-water fish prized for firm white flesh
summary_ja: 暖かい海に棲む大型魚の総称で、締まった白身は鍋や刺身に向く。水温の高い南方の海域に多く生息するため西日本の漁場で獲れやすく、クエをはじめ種類ごとに珍重される高級魚の一群。
summary_en: A broad family of large warm-water fish with firm white flesh suited to hot pot and sashimi. Concentrated in warmer southern waters, it is caught mainly off western Japan, with individual species like kue especially prized.

name_en: chicken grunt — a summer fish at its best just before spawning
summary_ja: 梅雨時期に脂が乗る白身魚で、「梅雨イサキ」と呼ばれ塩焼きや刺身で食べられる。産卵前に沿岸へ寄る性質があるため、この時期の内湾に面した港では水揚げが増え、脂の乗りも最も良くなるとされる。
summary_en: A white-fleshed fish that fattens ahead of the rainy season, earning the nickname 'tsuyu-isaki'. Served salt-grilled or raw — it moves inshore before spawning, so bay-facing ports see the biggest catch, and the best fat, at that time of year.

name_en: striped jack — a rare relative of the horse mackerel valued at sushi counters
summary_ja: アジ科の中でも高値で取引される高級魚で、天然物は希少。コリッとした食感の刺身が寿司ネタとして人気で、潮通しの良い穏やかな湾では養殖が発達し、天然物との身質の違いが語られる。
summary_en: One of the priciest fish in the jack family, especially scarce in the wild. Its crisp raw texture makes it a prized sushi topping — calm, well-flushed bays support aquaculture, and farmed fish are often compared against the rarer wild catch.

name_en: carp — a freshwater fish long simmered for hearty winter meals
summary_ja: 内陸の川魚で、うま煮や鯉こくとして冬に食べられてきた。泥臭さを抜く「臭み抜き」の技術が伝わり、湧水を利用した養魚池で育てるほど臭みが少なく、内陸の食文化を支える貴重なタンパク源とされてきた。
summary_en: An inland river fish long simmered for winter meals, whether as sweet-savory umani or miso-based koikoku soup. Know-how for purging its muddy notes is passed down, and spring-fed ponds raise fish with less of that flavor to begin with.

name_en: loach — a small mud-dwelling fish for skewers and hot pot
summary_ja: 水田や小川の泥に棲む細長い川魚で、丸のままの柳川鍋や、素焼きにして甘辛いたれで食べる。生命力が強く水質の変化に強いため、都市近郊の水路でも古くから庶民の味として親しまれてきた。
summary_en: A slender fish of paddy mud and streams, simmered whole in yanagawa-nabe hot pot or skewered plain and glazed sweet-savory. Hardy enough to survive poor water quality, it has long been an everyday fish even from canals near cities.

name_en: pond smelt — the fish of winter ice-hole fishing
summary_ja: 湖に棲む小魚で、冬の氷上穴釣りの対象として知られる。汽水湖など餌となるプランクトンが豊富な水域で群れをなし、丸ごと天ぷらや南蛮漬けにすると小骨まで気にせず食べられる。
summary_en: A small lake fish famous as the target of winter ice-hole fishing. It schools densely in brackish lakes rich in plankton feed, and is eaten whole as tempura or in sweet vinegar nanban-zuke, bones and all.

name_en: silver-stripe round herring — a small, silver-banded fish for sashimi and frying
summary_ja: 体側に銀色の帯を持つ小魚で、手開きにした刺身を菊の花のように盛る「菊花造り」で知られる。鮮度落ちが早いため島の周りの澄んだ海で獲れてすぐ食べる文化が根付き、鮮度が命の魚とされる。
summary_en: A small fish with a silver band down its flank, famously hand-filleted and fanned into a chrysanthemum-shaped sashimi platter. It spoils fast, so a culture of eating it the moment it's landed from clear island waters took hold.

name_en: whitebait — the tiny, translucent juveniles of sardine
summary_ja: イワシなどの稚魚を指し、釜揚げや天日干しのしらす干しとして、ご飯や大根おろしと合わせて食べられる。海底の地形が湧昇流を生む湾に面した漁港ほど群れが集まりやすく、水揚げの中心地となっている。
summary_en: The tiny, translucent juveniles of sardine and related fish. Kettle-boiled or sun-dried, served over rice or with grated daikon — bays where seabed topography drives upwelling currents draw the densest shoals and anchor the main fisheries.

name_en: moray eel — a fearsome-looking fish eaten deep-fried in Kochi
summary_ja: 見た目は獰猛だが、高知など一部地域では郷土料理として親しまれる魚で、から揚げやたたきで食べられる。硬い皮を持つため下処理に技術が要り、黒潮に近い漁場を持つ土地ほど食べる文化が根付いてきた。
summary_en: A fierce-looking fish that nonetheless features in the local cooking of places like Kochi, served deep-fried or seared as tataki. Its tough skin demands skilled prep, and Kuroshio-adjacent fishing towns are where the custom of eating it took hold.

name_en: broadbanded thornyhead — a rich, deep-red fish from northern deep waters
summary_ja: 北の海の深場に棲む赤い魚で、脂が非常に多く煮付けにすると濃厚な旨みが出る高級魚。冷たい深海に生息するため漁獲量が少なく、水深数百メートルの好漁場を持つ港でのみ安定して水揚げされる。
summary_en: A deep-red fish from the cold, deep waters of the north, exceptionally fatty and richly flavored when simmered. Living hundreds of meters down, it is caught in only limited numbers, and just a few ports with grounds that deep land it reliably.

name_en: Japanese seabass — a summer fish that changes its name as it grows
summary_ja: 成長で名前が変わる出世魚で、夏が旬。淡白な白身は洗いや塩焼きで食べられ、河口の汽水域で稚魚期を過ごすため、そうした湾の奥に面した港では出世魚としての漁が古くから続けられてきた。
summary_en: A 'shusseuo' whose name changes with size, at its best in summer. Its mild white flesh is served as chilled 'arai' or salt-grilled — it spends its juvenile stage in brackish river mouths, and ports at the head of such bays have long fished it as it grows.

name_en: tilefish — a delicate pink fish prized in Kyoto as 'guji'
summary_ja: 上品な甘みを持つピンク色の魚で、京都では「ぐじ」と呼ばれる。若狭湾で獲れたものに一塩を施し、鯖街道を通して京都まで運んだ歴史から、若狭の一塩ものが京料理で珍重されるようになった。
summary_en: A pink-skinned fish with a subtle sweetness, known in Kyoto as 'guji'. Fish caught in Wakasa Bay were lightly salted and carried inland along the old Saba Kaido route, a history that made lightly-salted Wakasa amadai prized in Kyoto cuisine.

name_en: swordfish — a lean, steak-like fish landed on Japan's Sanriku coast
summary_ja: 剣のように長く伸びた吻を持つ大型魚で、ステーキのような厚切りの切り身で照り焼きやフライにされる。近海はえ縄漁で獲れる三陸沖の漁場に面した港ほど水揚げが多く、全国有数の産地となっている。
summary_en: A large fish with a sword-like snout, cut into thick steak-like fillets and glazed teriyaki-style or fried. Ports facing the Sanriku fishing grounds, worked by coastal longline, land the most and rank among Japan's top sources.

name_en: icefish — a translucent, needle-thin fish of brackish lakes
summary_ja: 体が透き通った針のように細い魚で、踊り食いや卵とじで食べられる。汽水域の湖や川に春に群れをなすため、そうした湖のほとりの町では郷土の珍味「七珍」の一つとして古くから食されてきた。
summary_en: A translucent, needle-thin fish, sometimes eaten live or folded into egg. It schools each spring in brackish lakes and rivers, and lakeside towns there have long served it as one of their prized local 'seven delicacies'.

name_en: fat greenling — a rocky-shore fish whose liver is a local delicacy
summary_ja: 岩礁に棲む白身魚で、江戸前で刺身や煮付けにされる。動きが少なく居着く性質から地域ごとに味の違いが出やすく、東北の港では肝も珍味として食べられるなど、地魚として親しまれてきた。
summary_en: A white-fleshed fish of rocky shores, served raw or simmered in old Edomae style. Sedentary by nature, it varies by region, and in some Tohoku ports its liver is eaten too — a fish long prized as a local catch.

name_en: gurnard — a spiny, winged fish valued for its firm winter flesh
summary_ja: 胸びれを翼のように広げて海底を歩く魚で、冬に脂が乗る。上品な白身は刺身や潮汁で楽しまれ、海底が砂泥質の穏やかな内湾に多く生息するため、そうした港では地魚として昔から食べられてきた。
summary_en: A fish that spreads its wing-like pectoral fins to 'walk' along the seabed, fattening in winter. Its delicate white flesh goes into sashimi or clear soup, and it favors calm, sandy-bottomed bays, where it has long been eaten as a local catch.

name_en: mudskipper — the amphibious fish unique to the Ariake Sea
summary_ja: 有明海の干潟だけに生息する魚で、「がね漬け」や蒲焼で食べられる。干満差が国内最大級の干潟に生息域が限られるため他の海では代わりが利かず、突き漁という独自の漁法とともに地域の味として残った。
summary_en: A fish found only on the mudflats of the Ariake Sea, known for skipping across the mud on its fins and eaten simmered or grilled. Confined to the sea's uniquely vast tidal flats, it survives nowhere else, alongside a distinctive spear-jab fishing method.

name_en: sandfish — the winter fish that gives Akita its name-day thunder
summary_ja: 雷が鳴る初冬に沿岸へ押し寄せる魚で、秋田の県魚。しょっつる鍋やから揚げ、飯寿司で食べられ、産卵のため接岸する回遊の習性が「鰰」の字の由来ともなり、県を代表する冬の味覚として根付いている。
summary_en: A fish that surges toward shore with the first winter thunder — Akita's official prefectural fish. Eaten in shottsuru hot pot, deep-fried, or as izushi, its shoreward spawning run gave rise to its 'fish-thunder' kanji and its status as Akita's winter icon.

name_en: crucian carp — the fish behind Japan's oldest sushi
summary_ja: 琵琶湖固有種のニゴロブナを含む川魚で、米飯で乳酸発酵させる「ふなずし」は寿司の原型とされる。固有種が育つ湖でしか本来の味は出せないとされ、長期熟成させるなれずしの技術が今も受け継がれている。
summary_en: A river fish including the Lake Biwa-endemic nigorobuna, fermented with rice into funazushi, often called the ancestor of all sushi. Its true flavor is said to come only from the lake the endemic species calls home, sustaining an ancient narezushi craft.

name_en: catfish — a whiskered river fish revived as a regional specialty
summary_ja: ひげを持つ川魚で、地震を起こすとする俗信でも知られる。天ぷらや蒲焼で、うなぎの代替としても食べられ、水郷地帯の水路網が育てやすい環境となるため、養殖に取り組む町おこしの動きも見られる。
summary_en: A whiskered river fish, long associated in folklore with causing earthquakes. Served as tempura or grilled kabayaki-style, sometimes as an eel substitute — canal-laced water towns offer easy farming conditions, spurring local revival efforts.

name_en: filefish — a thin-skinned fish famous for its liver
summary_ja: 皮を丸ごと剥いで捌く魚で、それが名の由来ともなる。淡白な身と濃厚な肝を和えて食べる「肝あえ」が名物で、水温の低い時期ほど肝が肥大するため、冬場の産地では特に高値で取引される。
summary_en: A fish whose skin is peeled off whole in preparation — the source of its name. Its mild flesh is famously mixed with its rich liver as 'kimo-ae', and the liver swells largest in colder months, when winter catches fetch the highest prices.

name_en: butterfish — a flat, silvery fish for Kansai's New Year table
summary_ja: 菱形に近い平たい体を持つ白身魚で、関西では祝い魚として西京焼きや正月料理に使われる。骨が少なく脂も上品なため扱いやすく、瀬戸内海に面した産地では古くから縁起物の魚として重宝されてきた。
summary_en: A flat, diamond-shaped white-fleshed fish. In the Kansai region it serves as a celebratory fish, miso-glazed or featured at New Year — easy to prepare thanks to few bones and delicate fat, long valued as an auspicious catch along the Seto Inland Sea.
